definitions.explanation: The release of stored electrical energy, either as a natural phenomenon (like lightning) or in a device (like a battery losing its charge).

examples.japanese: バッテリーが{放電|ほうでん}した。
{静電気|せいでんき}の{放電|ほうでん}でパチッと{音|おと}がした。
examples.english: There was a crackling sound from the static electricity discharge.

examples.japanese: {長期間|ちょうきかん}{使|つか}わないと、バッテリーが{自然|しぜん}{放電|ほうでん}してしまうことがある。
examples.english: If left unused for a long time, the battery may naturally discharge on its own.

notes:
Compound of {放|ほう} (release) + {電|でん} (electricity). The opposite of {充電|じゅうでん} (charging).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {放電|ほうでん}する — to discharge (する verb)
- {自然|しぜん}{放電|ほうでん} — natural discharge, self-discharge
- {放電|ほうでん}{現象|げんしょう} — discharge phenomenon
- {過|か}{放電|ほうでん} — over-discharge (damaging a battery by draining it too far)

RELATED TERMS:
- {充電|じゅうでん} — charging (opposite)
- {蓄電|ちくでん} — storing electricity
- {感電|かんでん} — electric shock (receiving a discharge)
